        missed = set(range(self.n)) - present - {0}
        # assign missed greedily
        for m in missed:
            # put into cheapest feasible insertion among existing routes else new route
            best_delta = None
            best_place = None
            for idx, r in enumerate(cleaned):
                load = sum(self.demands[x] for x in r if x != 0)
                if load + self.demands[m] > self.vehicle_capacity:
                    continue
                for pos in range(1, len(r)):
                    before = self.distance_matrix[r[pos-1], r[pos]]
                    after = self.distance_matrix[r[pos-1], m] + self.distance_matrix[m, r[pos]]
                    delta = after - before
                    if frozenset((r[pos-1], m)) in self.forbidden_edges or frozenset((m, r[pos])) in self.forbidden_edges:
                        continue
                    if best_delta is None or delta < best_delta:
                        best_delta = delta
                        best_place = (idx, pos)
            if best_place is not None:
                cleaned[best_place[0]].insert(best_place[1], m)
            else:
                cleaned.append([0, m, 0])
        return cleaned

    def _extract_cuts(self, interface_solution, parts):
        """
        Return a set of cuts (unordered pairs) representing bad cross-boundary adjacency.
        parts: list of parts (node lists). We'll map node to part id for detection.
        """
        part_of = {}
        for pid, p in enumerate(parts):
            for node in p:
                part_of[node] = pid
        # compute average distance across solution edges (excluding depot->depot)
        edges = []
        for r in interface_solution:
            for a, b in zip(r[:-1], r[1:]):
                if a == 0 and b == 0:
                    continue
                edges.append(self.distance_matrix[a, b])
        avg = np.mean(edges) if len(edges) > 0 else 0.0
        cuts = set()
        for r in interface_solution:
            for a, b in zip(r[:-1], r[1:]):
                if a == 0 and b == 0:
                    continue
                if a == 0 or b == 0:
                    continue
                pa = part_of.get(a, -1)
                pb = part_of.get(b, -1)
                if pa != pb:
                    # cross-boundary adjacency; if it's relatively long, mark as cut
                    if self.distance_matrix[a, b] > max(1.2 * avg, np.median(edges) if len(edges) > 0 else 0):
                        cuts.add(frozenset((a, b)))
                    # count adjacency for possible contraction of pairs that often appear together (even across parts)
                    self.pair_counts[frozenset((a, b))] += 1
        return cuts

    def _apply_cuts_and_contract(self, cuts):
        # add cuts to forbidden edges
        for c in cuts:
            self.forbidden_edges.add(c)
        # attempt contraction for pairs with high counts: merge their groups so they stay together in partitions
        threshold = 3  # require occurrence in multiple iterations
        merged_any = False
        # Build a map from node to group index
        node_to_group = {}
        for gi, g in enumerate(self.groups):
            for node in g:
                node_to_group[node] = gi
        # iterate through pair_counts sorted by high counts
        items = sorted(self.pair_counts.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1])
        for pair, cnt in items:
            if cnt < threshold:
                break
            a, b = tuple(pair)
            ga = node_to_group.get(a, None)
            gb = node_to_group.get(b, None)
            if ga is None or gb is None or ga == gb:
                continue
            # merge smaller into larger group
            if len(self.groups[ga]) < len(self.groups[gb]):
                ga, gb = gb, ga
            # merge gb into ga
            self.groups[ga].extend(self.groups[gb])
            for nd in self.groups[gb]:
                node_to_group[nd] = ga
            self.groups[gb] = []
            merged_any = True
        if merged_any:
            # compact groups to remove empties
            self.groups = [g for g in self.groups if len(g) > 0]

    def _reoptimize_local(self, state_region_nodes, routes, time_limit=0.02):
        """
        Local reoptimization focused on routes that include nodes in state_region_nodes.
        Performs relocates and swaps within a short time limit.
        """
        start = time.time()
        changed = True
        while changed and (time.time() - start) < time_limit:
            changed = False
            # find routes that contain any targeted node
            target_routes = [i for i, r in enumerate(routes) if any(node in state_region_nodes for node in r)]
            for i in target_routes:
                for j in range(len(routes)):
                    if i == j:
                        continue
                    ri = routes[i]
                    rj = routes[j]
                    # try relocate from i to j
                    for pos in range(1, len(ri)-1):
                        cus = ri[pos]
                        if cus == 0:
                            continue
                        loadj = sum(self.demands[x] for x in rj if x != 0)
                        if loadj + self.demands[cus] > self.vehicle_capacity:
                            continue
                        best_pos = None
                        best_delta = 0
                        before_remove = self.distance_matrix[ri[pos-1], ri[pos]] + self.distance_matrix[ri[pos], ri[pos+1]]
                        after_remove = self.distance_matrix[ri[pos-1], ri[pos+1]]
                        remove_cost = after_remove - before_remove
                        for ins in range(1, len(rj)):
                            before_ins = self.distance_matrix[rj[ins-1], rj[ins]]
                            after_ins = self.distance_matrix[rj[ins-1], cus] + self.distance_matrix[cus, rj[ins]]
                            delta = remove_cost + (after_ins - before_ins)
                            if frozenset((rj[ins-1], cus)) in self.forbidden_edges or frozenset((cus, rj[ins])) in self.forbidden_edges:
                                continue
                            if delta < best_delta - 1e-8:
                                best_delta = delta
                                best_pos = ins
                        if best_pos is not None:
                            del routes[i][pos]
                            routes[j].insert(best_pos, cus)
                            changed = True
                            break
                    if changed:
                        break
                if changed:
                    break
        # clean routes
        cleaned = []
        for r in routes:
            if len(r) == 0:
                continue
            rr = [x for x in r]
            if rr[0] != 0:
                rr.insert(0, 0)
            if rr[-1] != 0:
                rr.append(0)
            if all(x == 0 for x in rr):
                continue
            cleaned.append(rr)
        return cleaned

    def _online_update(self, parts, interface_solution, cuts):
        """
        Update surrogate matrix using simple reinforcement:
        - reward edges inside parts that were used in good solution (decrease surrogate)
        - penalize edges corresponding to cuts (increase surrogate) so partitioner avoids them
        """
        # compute edge frequency inside parts in interface_solution
        used = defaultdict(int)
        for r in interface_solution:
            for a, b in zip(r[:-1], r[1:]):
                used[(a, b)] += 1
                used[(b, a)] += 1
        # shrink or grow surrogate entries
        for a in range(self.n):
            for b in range(self.n):
                if a == b:
                    continue
                key = (a, b)
                if used.get(key, 0) > 0:
                    # reward (lower surrogate)
                    self.surrogate[a, b] *= 0.995
                else:
                    # small decay
                    self.surrogate[a, b] *= 1.0005
        # penalize cuts strongly
        for c in cuts:
            a, b = tuple(c)
            self.surrogate[a, b] *= 1.2
            self.surrogate[b, a] *= 1.2
        # clip surrogate to reasonable range
        np.clip(self.surrogate, 1e-6, 1e6, out=self.surrogate)

    def _improved(self, cost):
        if cost < self.best_cost - 1e-8:
            self.best_cost = cost
            self.iter_since_improve = 0
            return True
        else:
            self.iter_since_improve += 1
            return False

    def _diversify_partition(self):
        # random perturbation of surrogate to escape stagnation: add small noise
        noise = np.random.normal(scale=0.1, size=self.surrogate.shape)
        self.surrogate += np.abs(noise)
        # also randomly split a large group if any
        big_idx = None
        for idx, g in enumerate(self.groups):
            if len(g) >= 6:
                big_idx = idx
                break
        if big_idx is not None:
            g = self.groups[big_idx]
            random.shuffle(g)
            mid = len(g) // 2
            self.groups[big_idx] = g[:mid]
            self.groups.append(g[mid:])

    def _expand_contracts_to_permutation(self, routes):
        """
        Expand groups if any contraction logic changed ordering.
        Our internal routes use original node indices, so just flatten.
        """
        flat = []
        for r in routes:
            if len(flat) == 0:
                flat.extend(r)
            else:
                # avoid double zero
                if flat[-1] == 0 and r[0] == 0:
                    flat.extend(r[1:])
                else:
                    flat.extend(r)
        # ensure correct formatting: each route starts and ends with 0
        if flat[0] != 0:
            flat.insert(0, 0)
        if flat[-1] != 0:
            flat.append(0)
        # ensure each customer visited exactly once; if duplicates or missing, fix greedily
        customers = [i for i in flat if i != 0]
        missing = [i for i in range(1, self.n) if i not in customers]
        # remove duplicates (keep first occurrence)
        seen = set()
        new_flat = []
        for x in flat:
            if x == 0:
                new_flat.append(0)
            else:
                if x in seen:
                    continue
                seen.add(x)
                new_flat.append(x)
        # append missing customers into new short routes
        for m in missing:
            new_flat.extend([0, m, 0])
        # clean possible consecutive zeros
        out = []
        for x in new_flat:
            if out and out[-1] == 0 and x == 0:
                continue
            out.append(x)
        if out[0] != 0:
            out.insert(0, 0)
        if out[-1] != 0:
            out.append(0)
        return out

    # --- main solve method implementing the overall loop ---
    def solve(self) -> list:
        """
        Solve the Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem (CVRP).

        Returns:
            A one-dimensional list of integers representing the sequence of nodes visited by all vehicles.
        """
        n = self.n
        # quick trivial case
        if n <= 2:
            return [0, 0] if n == 1 else [0, 1, 0]

        # initialize state and surrogate already in constructor
        # initial oracle: solve whole problem once to have baseline
        all_nodes = list(range(n))
        initial_routes = self._clarke_wright(all_nodes)
        initial_cost = self._routes_cost(initial_routes)
        self.best_cost = initial_cost
        self.best_routes = initial_routes
        self.iter_since_improve = 0

        # time / iteration budget
        max_iters = max(10, int(5 + np.sqrt(n) * 3))
        start_time = time.time()
        time_budget = max(1.0, 0.01 * n)  # seconds
        iter_count = 0

        while iter_count < max_iters and (time.time() - start_time) < time_budget:
            iter_count += 1
            # Partition groups -> parts
            parts = self._partition(self.surrogate)
            # Solve each part independently
            solutions = {}
            for p in parts:
                key = tuple(sorted(p))
                # Solve oracle on expanded node list (include depot)
                sol = self._clarke_wright(p)
                solutions[key] = sol
            # Merge with interface optimization
            merged_routes = self._merge_with_interface_opt(parts, solutions, time_limit=0.05)
            merged_cost = self._routes_cost(merged_routes)
            # Extract cuts across partitions
            cuts = self._extract_cuts(merged_routes, parts)
            # Apply cuts and possibly contract groups
            self._apply_cuts_and_contract(cuts)
            # Reopt local: use nodes involved in cuts as affected region
            affected_nodes = set()
            for c in cuts:
                a, b = tuple(c)
                affected_nodes.add(a)
                affected_nodes.add(b)
            if len(affected_nodes) > 0:
                merged_routes = self._reoptimize_local(affected_nodes, merged_routes, time_limit=0.03)
                merged_cost = self._routes_cost(merged_routes)
            # Online update surrogate
            self._online_update(parts, merged_routes, cuts)
            # update best
            improved = self._improved(merged_cost)
            if improved:
                self.best_routes = [list(r) for r in merged_routes]
            # stagnation?
            if self.iter_since_improve >= 3:
                self._diversify_partition()
                self.iter_since_improve = 0  # reset after diversification

        # final expansion to flattened permutation
        final_perm = self._expand_contracts_to_permutation(self.best_routes if self.best_routes is not None else initial_routes)
        # ensure feasibility: check capacity and each visited exactly once; if not, fallback to simple greedy split
        valid = True
        seen = set()
        route = []
        cur_load = 0
        for node in final_perm:
            if node == 0:
                if len(route) > 0:
                    if cur_load > self.vehicle_capacity:
                        valid = False
                    route = []
                    cur_load = 0
            else:
                if node in seen:
                    valid = False
                seen.add(node)
                cur_load += self.demands[node]
                if cur_load > self.vehicle_capacity:
                    valid = False
        if not valid or len(seen) != n - 1:
            # fallback simple feasible greedy construction
            solution = [0]
            cur_cap = 0
            for i in range(1, n):
                if cur_cap + self.demands[i] > self.vehicle_capacity:
                    solution.append(0)
                    cur_cap = 0
                solution.append(i)
                cur_cap += self.demands[i]
            if solution[-1] != 0:
                solution.append(0)
            return solution

        return final_perm

# Your key function here
def _two_opt(self, tour, it_limit=100):
    """
    Optimized 2-opt local improvement (best-improvement strategy).

    Performs repeated best 2-edge-exchange improvements until no improving
    move is found or iteration limit is reached. Uses local variables to
    minimize attribute lookups and avoids unnecessary work when the tour is small.
    """
    n = len(tour)
    if n < 3:
        return list(tour)

    dmat = self.distance_matrix
    tour = list(tour)  # work on a mutable copy

    it = 0
    eps = 1e-12
    while it < it_limit:
        it += 1
        best_delta = -eps
        best_i = -1
        best_j = -1

        # search for the best improving 2-opt move
        # we avoid checking the trivial swap that breaks the tour (i==0 and j==n-1)
        for i in range(0, n - 2):
            a = tour[i]
            b = tour[i + 1]
            # j starts at i+2 to ensure non-overlapping edges
            # j can be n-1 (connects to tour[0] when computing dnode)
            for j in range(i + 2, n):
                if i == 0 and j == n - 1:
                    continue
                c = tour[j]
                dnode = tour[j + 1] if (j + 1) < n else tour[0]
                # compute change in length if we replace edges (a-b) & (c-dnode)
                # with (a-c) & (b-dnode)
                delta = (dmat[a, c] + dmat[b, dnode]) - (dmat[a, b] + dmat[c, dnode])
                if delta < best_delta:
                    best_delta = delta
                    best_i = i
                    best_j = j

        # apply the best found improvement (if any)
        if best_i >= 0:
            i = best_i
            j = best_j
            # reverse the segment (i+1 .. j) in-place
            tour[i + 1:j + 1] = tour[i + 1:j + 1][::-1]
        else:
            break

    return tour

# Your key function here
def _merge_with_interface_opt(self, parts, solutions, time_limit=0.05):
    """
    Merge part solutions and perform local interface optimization across routes.
    Optimized implementation: keeps an index (pos map) of customer -> (route_idx, pos)
    and route loads to avoid repeated scans. Minimizes attribute lookups by local
    variable aliasing.
    """
    # collect all routes
    all_routes = []
    for p in parts:
        key = tuple(sorted(p))
        r = solutions.get(key, [])
        all_routes.extend([list(rr) for rr in r])

    # aliases for speed
    dm = self.distance_matrix
    demands = self.demands
    cap = self.vehicle_capacity
    forbidden = self.forbidden_edges

    # build route loads and position map: customer -> (route_idx, pos_idx)
    route_loads = []
    pos = {}  # node -> (route_idx, idx_in_route)
    for ri, r in enumerate(all_routes):
        load = 0
        for idx, node in enumerate(r):
            if node != 0:
                load += demands[node]
                pos[node] = (ri, idx)
        route_loads.append(load)

    start = time.time()
    improved = True
    # local references for performance
    time_fn = time.time
    while improved and (time_fn() - start) < time_limit:
        improved = False

        # RELOCATE: iterate over a snapshot of customers to avoid mutation issues
        for cus in list(pos.keys()):
            # ensure cus still present in pos (may have been moved)
            if cus not in pos:
                continue
            ri, pidx = pos[cus]
            # route may have been removed/changed; guard
            if ri >= len(all_routes):
                continue
            r = all_routes[ri]
            # validate index
            if pidx <= 0 or pidx >= len(r) - 1 or r[pidx] != cus:
                # recalc pos from route if inconsistent (fallback)
                try:
                    pidx = r.index(cus)
                    pos[cus] = (ri, pidx)
                except ValueError:
                    pos.pop(cus, None)
                    continue
            # compute remove cost: (after_remove - before_remove)
            left, right = r[pidx - 1], r[pidx + 1]
            remove_cost = dm[left, right] - (dm[left, cus] + dm[cus, right])

            # attempt moving cus to other routes
            moved = False
            for j_route in range(len(all_routes)):
                if j_route == ri:
                    continue
                if route_loads[j_route] + demands[cus] > cap:
                    continue
                target = all_routes[j_route]
                best_delta = 0.0
                best_pos = None
                # iterate possible insertion positions in target
                # (1 .. len(target)-1) are valid insertion positions between nodes
                for ins_pos in range(1, len(target)):
                    left_t = target[ins_pos - 1]
                    right_t = target[ins_pos]
                    # forbidden adjacency checks
                    if frozenset((left_t, cus)) in forbidden or frozenset((cus, right_t)) in forbidden:
                        continue
                    ins_cost = (dm[left_t, cus] + dm[cus, right_t]) - dm[left_t, right_t]
                    delta = remove_cost + ins_cost
                    if delta < best_delta - 1e-8:
                        best_delta = delta
                        best_pos = ins_pos
                if best_pos is not None:
                    # perform move: remove from current route and insert into target
                    # Remove from r
                    del r[pidx]
                    route_loads[ri] -= demands[cus]
                    pos.pop(cus, None)
                    # update positions in r for nodes after pidx
                    for idx in range(pidx, len(r)):
                        node = r[idx]
                        if node != 0:
                            pos[node] = (ri, idx)
                    # Insert into target
                    target.insert(best_pos, cus)
                    route_loads[j_route] += demands[cus]
                    # update positions in target for nodes from best_pos to end
                    for idx in range(best_pos, len(target)):
                        node = target[idx]
                        if node != 0:
                            pos[node] = (j_route, idx)
                    moved = True
                    improved = True
                    break
            if moved:
                # break outer loop to restart search (greedy improvement)
                break

        if improved:
            # restart relocate phase
            continue

        # SIMPLE 2-OPT WITHIN EACH ROUTE (try the most improving single move)
        twoopt_done = False
        for idx, r in enumerate(all_routes):
            L = len(r)
            if L <= 4:
                continue
            # try all a,b pairs (positions in route) with 1..L-2 and a<b
            improved_in_route = False
            for a in range(1, L - 2):
                # bound b to keep small for time; but maintain correctness by full search
                for b in range(a + 1, L - 1):
                    i1, i2 = r[a - 1], r[a]
                    j1, j2 = r[b], r[b + 1]
                    delta = dm[i1, j1] + dm[i2, j2] - (dm[i1, i2] + dm[j1, j2])
                    if delta < -1e-8:
                        # check forbidden adjacencies that would result
                        if frozenset((i1, j1)) in forbidden or frozenset((i2, j2)) in forbidden:
                            continue
                        # apply reversal
                        r[a:b + 1] = reversed(r[a:b + 1])
                        # update pos map for affected nodes
                        for off in range(a, b + 1):
                            node = r[off]
                            if node != 0:
                                pos[node] = (idx, off)
                        improved = True
                        improved_in_route = True
                        twoopt_done = True
                        break
                if improved_in_route:
                    break
            if twoopt_done:
                break

    # clean empty or trivial routes
    cleaned = []
    for r in all_routes:
        rr = [x for x in r]
        if len(rr) == 0:
            continue
        if rr[0] != 0:
            rr.insert(0, 0)
        if rr[-1] != 0:
            rr.append(0)
        # drop routes that only have depot
        if all(x == 0 for x in rr):
            continue
        cleaned.append(rr)

    # ensure all customers present exactly once
    present = set()
    for r in cleaned:
        for x in r:
            if x != 0:
                present.add(x)
    missed = set(range(self.n)) - present - {0}
    # assign missed greedily
    for m in missed:
        best_delta = None
        best_place = None
        for idx, r in enumerate(cleaned):
            load = sum(self.demands[x] for x in r if x != 0)
            if load + self.demands[m] > self.vehicle_capacity:
                continue
            for pos_ins in range(1, len(r)):
                before = dm[r[pos_ins - 1], r[pos_ins]]
                after = dm[r[pos_ins - 1], m] + dm[m, r[pos_ins]]
                delta = after - before
                if frozenset((r[pos_ins - 1], m)) in self.forbidden_edges or frozenset((m, r[pos_ins])) in self.forbidden_edges:
                    continue
                if best_delta is None or delta < best_delta:
                    best_delta = delta
                    best_place = (idx, pos_ins)
        if best_place is not None:
            cleaned[best_place[0]].insert(best_place[1], m)
        else:
            cleaned.append([0, m, 0])
    return cleaned

algorithm RecursivePartitionCoordinator(problem, params)
    parts ← Partition(problem, params.initial_partitioning)                       // spatial/structural decomposition
    cache ← InitCache(); incumbent ← null; iter ← 0
    while not Terminate(iter, params)
        sub_solutions ← ∅
        for each part in parts
            sub_solutions[part] ← cache.get(part) or SolveSubproblem(part, params.subsolver) // exact/heuristic per part
        boundary_model ← BuildBoundaryModel(parts, sub_solutions, problem)       // small meta-instance linking parts
        coordinator_decision ← SolveCoordinator(boundary_model, params.coordinator) // flow/matching/assignment
        candidate ← AssembleSolution(sub_solutions, coordinator_decision)
        candidate ← ProjectAndRepair(candidate, problem)                         // global feasibility projection
        candidate.score ← Evaluate(candidate, problem); incumbent ← Best(incumbent, candidate)
        hotspots ← DetectFailureOrHighCostZones(candidate, problem)              // where decomposition hurts
        if ConvergedOrLimitReached(incumbent, iter, params) then return Decode(incumbent, problem)
        parts ← AdaptPartitioning(parts, hotspots, params)                       // split/merge/refocus regions
        UpdateCache(cache, parts, sub_solutions); iter ← iter + 1
    end while
    return Decode(incumbent, problem)

import numpy as np
import time
from collections import defaultdict

class TSPSolver:
    def __init__(self, coordinates: np.ndarray, distance_matrix: np.ndarray):
        """
        Initialize the TSP solver.

        Args:
            coordinates: Numpy array of shape (n, 2) containing the (x, y) coordinates of each city.
            distance_matrix: Numpy array of shape (n, n) containing pairwise distances between cities.
        """
        self.coordinates = coordinates
        self.distance_matrix = distance_matrix
        self.n = len(coordinates)
        # Parameters (tunable)
        self.params = {
            "initial_parts": 8,            # initial number of partitions
            "max_iters": 100,              # maximum iterations
            "time_limit": 30.0,            # seconds overall
            "subsolver_iters": 200,        # iterations / evaluation budget for 2-opt per subproblem
            "coordinator_iters": 200,      # iterations for coordinator 2-opt on parts
            "hotspot_threshold_factor": 1.5,  # factor above mean edge length to consider hotspot
            "min_part_size": 3,            # do not split below this
            "max_part_size": 200,          # try to keep parts below this
            "boundary_k": 5,               # number of boundary candidates per part (unused heavy)
            "no_improve_limit": 10         # iterations with no improvement to stop
        }

    # --- helper methods implementing pseudocode components ---

    def _initial_partition(self, k):
        # Partition by recursive splitting along longest axis at median, produce k parts
        indices = np.arange(self.n)
        parts = [indices.tolist()]

        def split_part(part):
            pts = self.coordinates[part]
            mins = pts.min(axis=0)
            maxs = pts.max(axis=0)
            span = maxs - mins
            axis = int(np.argmax(span))
            # sort by axis coordinate
            sorted_idx = sorted(part, key=lambda i: self.coordinates[i, axis])
            mid = len(sorted_idx) // 2
            return sorted_idx[:mid], sorted_idx[mid:]

    def _two_opt(self, tour, iters=1000, time_limit=None):
        """
        Best-improvement 2-opt variant.
        Same inputs/outputs as original but scans all possible 2-opt moves in an
        improvement pass and applies the single best move (largest decrease).
        Uses in-place two-pointer reversal to avoid creating intermediate lists.
        """
        if tour is None or len(tour) < 4:
            return tour
        # Ensure mutable list
        tour = list(tour)
        dm = self.distance_matrix
        n = len(tour)
        start_time = time.time()
        iter_count = 0
        improved = True
        eps = 1e-9

        while improved and iter_count < iters:
            if time_limit and (time.time() - start_time) > time_limit:
                break
            improved = False
            best_delta = -eps
            best_i = best_j = -1

            # Find the best single 2-opt move (largest negative delta)
            for i in range(n - 1):
                a = tour[i]
                b = tour[i + 1]
                d_a = dm[a]
                d_b = dm[b]
                dab = d_a[b]
                # Avoid removing the start edge-to-end when i == 0 (keep cycle)
                j_end = n if i > 0 else n - 1
                for j in range(i + 2, j_end):
                    c = tour[j]
                    dnode = tour[(j + 1) % n]
                    # delta = dist(a,c) + dist(b,d) - dist(a,b) - dist(c,d)
                    delta = d_a[c] + d_b[dnode] - dab - dm[c][dnode]
                    if delta < best_delta:
                        best_delta = delta
                        best_i = i
                        best_j = j

            # If a improving move was found, apply it (reverse segment i+1..j)
            if best_i >= 0:
                i = best_i
                j = best_j
                l = i + 1
                r = j
                # two-pointer in-place reversal
                while l < r:
                    tour[l], tour[r] = tour[r], tour[l]
                    l += 1
                    r -= 1
                improved = True

            iter_count += 1

        return tour

    def _solve_subproblem(self, part):

        # Return tour as list (cycle)
        if len(part) <= 1:

        for i in range(pcnt):

        return {"centroids": centroids, "cdist": cdist}

    def _solve_coordinator(self, boundary_model):

        pcnt = len(boundary_model["centroids"])

        nodes = list(range(pcnt))

        cdist = boundary_model["cdist"]

        iters = 0

            for i in range(len(tour) - 1):
                a = tour[i]
                b = tour[i + 1]
                for j in range(i + 2, len(tour) if i > 0 else len(tour) - 1):
                    c = tour[j]
                    dnode = tour[(j + 1) % len(tour)]
                    delta = (cdist[a, c] + cdist[b, dnode]) - (cdist[a, b] + cdist[c, dnode])
                    if delta < -1e-9:
                        tour[i + 1:j + 1] = reversed(tour[i + 1:j + 1])
                        improved = True
                        break
                if improved:

        return tour

    def _assemble_solution(self, parts, sub_solutions, coordinator_order):
        # Assemble by concatenating sub tours in coordinator order, connecting by best boundary nodes
        if not coordinator_order:
            # fallback: concatenate by part order
            sequences = [sub_solutions[tuple(sorted(p))] for p in parts]
            assembled = []
            for seq in sequences:
                assembled.extend(seq)

        assembled = list(sub_solutions[tuple(sorted(parts[coordinator_order[0]]))])
        for idx in coordinator_order[1:]:

            best_combo = None

            cand_a = assembled[-8:] if len(assembled) > 8 else assembled
            # try rotations of next_seq (start positions)
            max_try = min(8, len(next_seq))
            for i_a, a_node in enumerate(cand_a):
                # actual index in assembled
                idx_a = assembled.index(a_node)
                a_next = assembled[(idx_a + 1) % len(assembled)]
                for r in range(max_try):
                    j = r
                    b_node = next_seq[j]
                    b_next = next_seq[(j + 1) % len(next_seq)]
                    # cost change: remove edges (a_node->a_next) and (b_node->b_next), add (a_node->b_node) and (b_next->a_next)
                    delta = (self.distance_matrix[a_node, b_node] + self.distance_matrix[b_next, a_next]) - (self.distance_matrix[a_node, a_next] + self.distance_matrix[b_node, b_next])
                    if delta < best_delta:

            if best_combo is None:
                # fallback: simple append
                # rotate next_seq so its first is nearest to last of assembled
                last = assembled[-1]
                best_j = min(range(len(next_seq)), key=lambda j: self.distance_matrix[last, next_seq[j]])
                next_seq = next_seq[best_j:] + next_seq[:best_j]
                assembled.extend(next_seq)
            else:
                ia, jb = best_combo
                # perform merge: rotate assembled so ia is at end, rotate next_seq so jb+1 is start, then splice
                assembled = assembled[ia+1:] + assembled[:ia+1]
                # rotate next_seq so that jb+1 is start (so we break between jb and jb+1)
                next_seq = next_seq[jb+1:] + next_seq[:jb+1]
                assembled.extend(next_seq)

        seen = set(assembled)
        if len(assembled) != self.n or len(seen) != len(assembled):
            # repair: create permutation by taking unique in order then append missing
            unique = []
            seen = set()
            for v in assembled:
                if v not in seen:
                    unique.append(v)
                    seen.add(v)
            missing = [i for i in range(self.n) if i not in seen]
            unique.extend(missing)
            assembled = unique
        return assembled

    def _project_and_repair(self, candidate):
        # Ensure it's a valid permutation and improve with global 2-opt
        # candidate: list of nodes
        n = self.n
        seen = set(candidate)
        if len(candidate) != n or len(seen) != n:
            # repair by retaining first occurrence of each, then append missing
            unique = []
            seen = set()
            for v in candidate:
                if v not in seen and 0 <= v < n:
                    unique.append(v)
                    seen.add(v)
            missing = [i for i in range(n) if i not in seen]
            unique.extend(missing)
            candidate = unique
        # apply global two-opt
        candidate = self._two_opt(candidate, iters=1000, time_limit=1.0)  # small time limit
        return candidate

    def _evaluate(self, tour):
        return self._tour_length(tour)

    def _detect_hotspots(self, tour):
        # Identify edges much longer than average and map them to parts by node membership
        if tour is None or len(tour) < 2:
            return set()
        edges = []
        d = self.distance_matrix
        for i in range(len(tour)):
            a = tour[i]
            b = tour[(i + 1) % len(tour)]
            edges.append(d[a, b])
        edges = np.array(edges)
        mean = edges.mean()
        threshold = mean * self.params["hotspot_threshold_factor"]
        hotspots_idx = np.where(edges > threshold)[0]
        hotspots_nodes = set()
        for idx in hotspots_idx:
            hotspots_nodes.add(tour[idx])
            hotspots_nodes.add(tour[(idx + 1) % len(tour)])
        return hotspots_nodes

    def _adapt_partitioning(self, parts, hotspots):
        # Split parts that contain hotspot nodes and are large enough
        new_parts = []
        for p in parts:
            pset = set(p)
            if len(p) > self.params["min_part_size"] and (pset & hotspots):
                # split along longest axis at median for the nodes in p
                a, b = self._split_for_part(p)
                if len(a) == 0 or len(b) == 0:

                else:
                    new_parts.append(a)
                    new_parts.append(b)
            else:
                new_parts.append(p)

        merged = []
        smalls = [p for p in new_parts if len(p) < max(2, self.params["min_part_size"])]
        larges = [p for p in new_parts if len(p) >= max(2, self.params["min_part_size"])]
        merged = larges.copy()
        for sp in smalls:

                merged.append(sp)
                continue
            # find closest large part by centroid distance
            sc = np.array([self.coordinates[i] for i in sp]).mean(axis=0)
            best_idx = min(range(len(merged)), key=lambda j: np.linalg.norm(self.coordinates[merged[j]].mean(axis=0) - sc) if len(merged[j])>0 else float('inf'))
            merged[best_idx] = merged[best_idx] + sp
        return merged

    def _split_for_part(self, part):
        pts = self.coordinates[part]
        mins = pts.min(axis=0)
        maxs = pts.max(axis=0)
        span = maxs - mins
        axis = int(np.argmax(span))
        sorted_idx = sorted(part, key=lambda i: self.coordinates[i, axis])
        mid = len(sorted_idx) // 2
        return sorted_idx[:mid], sorted_idx[mid:]

    def _update_cache(self, cache, parts, sub_solutions):
        # Cache keyed by sorted tuple of part indices
        new_cache = {}
        for p in parts:
            key = tuple(sorted(p))
            if key in sub_solutions:
                new_cache[key] = sub_solutions[key]
            elif key in cache:
                new_cache[key] = cache[key]

    def _decode(self, incumbent):
        # Return numpy array permutation
        if incumbent is None:

        if len(arr) != self.n or set(arr.tolist()) != set(range(self.n)):

            return np.arange(self.n)

    def solve(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """
        Solve the Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP).

        Returns:

import numpy as np

class CVRPSolver:
    def __init__(self, coordinates: np.ndarray, distance_matrix: np.ndarray, demands: list, vehicle_capacity: int):
        """
        Initialize the CVRP solver.

        Args:
            coordinates: Numpy array of shape (n, 2) containing the (x, y) coordinates of each node, including the depot.
            distance_matrix: Numpy array of shape (n, n) containing pairwise distances between nodes.
            demands: List of integers representing the demand of each node (first node is typically the depot with zero demand).
            vehicle_capacity: Integer representing the maximum capacity of each vehicle.

    def _total_demand(self, nodes):
        return sum(self.demands[i] for i in nodes)

    def _euclid_dist(self, i, j):
        return self.distance_matrix[i, j]

    def _kmeans_partition(self, node_indices, k, max_it=20):
        # Simple k-means on coordinates (excluding depot if present)
        if k <= 0 or len(node_indices) == 0:
            return []
        coords = self.coordinates[node_indices]
        # initialize centers by sampling nodes
        centers_idx = random.sample(range(len(node_indices)), min(k, len(node_indices)))
        centers = coords[centers_idx, :].copy()
        for _ in range(max_it):
            clusters = [[] for _ in range(k)]
            for idx, p in enumerate(coords):
                # assign to nearest center
                dists = np.sum((centers - p) ** 2, axis=1)
                clusters[int(np.argmin(dists))].append(node_indices[idx])
            new_centers = []
            changed = False
            for cluster in clusters:
                if len(cluster) == 0:
                    # reinit empty center
                    new_centers.append(coords[random.randrange(len(coords))])
                    continue
                c = np.mean(self.coordinates[cluster], axis=0)
                new_centers.append(c)
            new_centers = np.array(new_centers)
            if np.allclose(new_centers, centers):
                break
            centers = new_centers
        # filter empty clusters and return list of parts
        parts = [cluster for cluster in clusters if len(cluster) > 0]
        return parts

    def _split_part_by_axis(self, part_nodes):
        # split by projecting onto principal axis (approx by farthest pair)
        if len(part_nodes) <= 1:
            return [part_nodes]
        coords = self.coordinates[part_nodes]
        # find farthest pair
        maxd = -1
        a, b = 0, 0
        for i in range(min(10, len(coords))):
            for j in range(i+1, min(10, len(coords))):
                d = np.sum((coords[i] - coords[j])**2)
                if d > maxd:
                    maxd = d
                    a, b = i, j
        if maxd <= 0:
            # fallback split by median x
            xs = coords[:, 0]
            order = np.argsort(xs)
            mid = len(order) // 2
            return [ [part_nodes[int(i)] for i in order[:mid] ], [part_nodes[int(i)] for i in order[mid:]] ]
        # axis vector
        axis = coords[b] - coords[a]
        if np.allclose(axis, 0):
            xs = coords[:, 0]
            order = np.argsort(xs)
            mid = len(order) // 2
            return [ [part_nodes[int(i)] for i in order[:mid] ], [part_nodes[int(i)] for i in order[mid:]] ]
        # project and split median
        projections = (coords - coords[a]).dot(axis)

        mid = len(order) // 2
        part1 = [part_nodes[int(i)] for i in order[:mid]]
        part2 = [part_nodes[int(i)] for i in order[mid:]]

    def _solve_subproblem_greedy(self, nodes):
        # Solve VRP on given nodes (list of customer indices, excluding depot 0)
        # Return list of routes, each route is list of nodes starting and ending with depot 0
        if len(nodes) == 0:
            return []
        # simple first-fit decreasing by demand: pack nodes into routes then order intra-route by nearest neighbor
        nodes_sorted = sorted(nodes, key=lambda i: -self.demands[i])
        routes = []
        loads = []
        for node in nodes_sorted:
            placed = False
            for r_idx, load in enumerate(loads):

                    routes[r_idx].append(node)
                    loads[r_idx] += self.demands[node]
                    placed = True

            if not placed:
                routes.append([node])
                loads.append(self.demands[node])
        # order nodes within each route by nearest neighbor heuristic starting from depot
        final_routes = []
        for r in routes:
            if len(r) == 0:

            unvisited = set(r)
            cur = 0
            seq = [0]
            while unvisited:
                # choose nearest from cur
                next_node = min(unvisited, key=lambda j: self._euclid_dist(cur, j))

        # Assign parts to vehicles by greedy nearest-centroid route creation.
        m = len(parts)
        if m == 0:
            return [[] for _ in range(min_vehicles)]
        used = [False] * m
        part_to_vehicle = [-1] * m
        vehicle_assignments = [[] for _ in range(min_vehicles)]
        # start each vehicle at depot (centroid of depot)
        for v in range(min_vehicles):
            # pick largest unassigned part by demand to seed
            candidates = [i for i in range(m) if not used[i]]
            if not candidates:

            seed = max(candidates, key=lambda i: self._total_demand(parts[i]))
            vehicle_assignments[v].append(seed)
            part_to_vehicle[seed] = v
            used[seed] = True
        # assign remaining greedily by nearest centroid to last assigned in vehicle
        while not all(used):
            progress = False
            for v in range(min_vehicles):
                # last centroid

                last = vehicle_assignments[v][-1]
                # find nearest unused part

                nearest = min(unused, key=lambda i: np.sum((centroids[i] - centroids[last])**2))

            if not progress:

                        for v in range(min_vehicles):

                cur_route.append(token)
                cur_load += self.demands[token]
        if cur_route:
            routes.append(cur_route)
        # try to insert missing into routes
        for node in missing:
            placed = False
            for r in routes:
                load = sum(self.demands[i] for i in r)
                if load + self.demands[node] <= self.vehicle_capacity:
                    # place by nearest insertion (find position minimizing added distance)
                    best_pos = 0
                    best_cost = None
                    seq = [0] + r + [0]
                    for pos in range(1, len(seq)):
                        prev = seq[pos-1]
                        nxt = seq[pos]
                        added = self._euclid_dist(prev, node) + self._euclid_dist(node, nxt) - self._euclid_dist(prev, nxt)
                        if best_cost is None or added < best_cost:
                            best_cost = added
                            best_pos = pos-1
                    r.insert(best_pos, node)
                    placed = True
                    break
            if not placed:
                # create new route
                routes.append([node])
        # convert routes back to flat list with depot separators
        flat = []
        for r in routes:
            flat.append(0)
            flat.extend(r)
            flat.append(0)
        # remove consecutive zeros
        compressed = []
        for x in flat:
            if compressed and compressed[-1] == 0 and x == 0:
                continue
            compressed.append(x)
        if compressed[-1] != 0:
            compressed.append(0)
        # final sanity: ensure all customers present
        present = set(i for i in compressed if i != 0)
        missing2 = set(range(1, n)) - present
        if missing2:
            # append missing as individual routes
            for node in missing2:
                compressed.extend([0, node, 0])
        # remove duplicates final check (keep first occurrence)
        final = []
        seen = set()
        for token in compressed:
            if token == 0:
                final.append(0)
            else:
                if token in seen:
                    continue
                seen.add(token)
                final.append(token)
        if final[-1] != 0:
            final.append(0)
        return final

    def _evaluate(self, flat_solution):
        # compute total distance
        total = 0.0
        prev = None
        for node in flat_solution:
            if prev is None:
                prev = node
                continue
            total += self._euclid_dist(prev, node)
            prev = node
        return total

    def _detect_hotspots(self, parts, cache, candidate_flat):
        # identify parts whose nodes ended up in many separated routes or have high local cost
        # heuristic: parts that required >1 route when solved from cache (or when their internal demand > capacity)
        hotspots = set()
        for idx, part in enumerate(parts):
            if len(part) == 0:
                continue
            key = frozenset(part)
            routes = cache.get(key)
            if routes is None:
                # if demand exceeds capacity, it's a hotspot
                if self._total_demand(part) > self.vehicle_capacity:
                    hotspots.add(idx)
            else:
                if len(routes) > 1:
                    hotspots.add(idx)
        # also check large edge jumps in candidate indicating boundary pain
        seq = candidate_flat
        for i in range(1, len(seq)):
            a = seq[i-1]
            b = seq[i]
            if a != 0 and b != 0:
                if self._euclid_dist(a, b) > np.mean(self.distance_matrix) * 1.5:
                    # find which part contains a or b and mark
                    for idx, part in enumerate(parts):
                        if a in part or b in part:
                            hotspots.add(idx)
        return list(hotspots)

    def _adapt_partitioning(self, parts, hotspots):
        # For each hotspot, split into two; also merge tiny parts
        new_parts = []
        hotspot_set = set(hotspots)
        for idx, part in enumerate(parts):
            if idx in hotspot_set and len(part) > 1:
                split = self._split_part_by_axis(part)
                for s in split:
                    if len(s) > 0:
                        new_parts.append(s)
            else:
                new_parts.append(part)
        # merge very small parts (singletons) with nearest centroid
        small_parts = [p for p in new_parts if 0 < len(p) <= 1]
        large_parts = [p for p in new_parts if len(p) > 1]
        if small_parts:
            centroids_large = [np.mean(self.coordinates[p], axis=0) for p in large_parts] if large_parts else []
            for sp in small_parts:
                if not large_parts:
                    large_parts.append(sp)
                    continue
                c_sp = np.mean(self.coordinates[sp], axis=0)
                # find nearest large part by centroid
                nearest = min(range(len(centroids_large)), key=lambda i: np.sum((centroids_large[i] - c_sp)**2))
                large_parts[nearest].extend(sp)
                # update centroid
                centroids_large[nearest] = np.mean(self.coordinates[large_parts[nearest]], axis=0)
        return large_parts

    def solve(self) -> list:
        """
        Solve the Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem (CVRP).

        Returns:
            A one-dimensional list of integers representing the sequence of nodes visited by all vehicles.
        """
        n = len(self.coordinates)
        # parameters for recursive coordinator loop
        max_iters = 30
        patience = 6  # iterations with no improvement before stopping
        random.seed(0)

        # initial partitioning: exclude depot (index 0)
        customer_nodes = [i for i in range(1, n)]
        total_demand = sum(self.demands[1:])
        min_vehicles = max(1, math.ceil(total_demand / self.vehicle_capacity))

        # choose initial number of parts as min_vehicles (spatial buckets)
        initial_k = max(1, min(len(customer_nodes), min_vehicles))
        parts = self._kmeans_partition(customer_nodes, initial_k)

        cache = dict()
        incumbent = None
        incumbent_score = float('inf')
        iter_no_improve = 0
        iter = 0

        while iter < max_iters:
            # solve subproblems per part (store in cache keyed by frozenset of nodes)
            for p_idx, part in enumerate(parts):
                key = frozenset(part)
                if key not in cache:
                    # solve
                    cache[key] = self._solve_subproblem_greedy(part)

            # build boundary model and solve coordinator
            centroids = self._build_boundary_model(parts)
            assignments = self._solve_coordinator_greedy(centroids, parts, min_vehicles)

            # assemble candidate solution by grouping parts assigned to vehicles and solving those unions
            candidate_flat = self._assemble_solution_from_assignment(assignments, parts, cache)

            # project and repair for feasibility
            candidate_flat = self._project_and_repair(candidate_flat)

            # evaluate
            score = self._evaluate(candidate_flat)
            if score < incumbent_score:
                incumbent = candidate_flat.copy()
                incumbent_score = score
                iter_no_improve = 0
            else:
                iter_no_improve += 1

            # convergence check
            if iter_no_improve >= patience:
                break

            # detect hotspots
            hotspots = self._detect_hotspots(parts, cache, candidate_flat)

            # adapt partitioning
            new_parts = self._adapt_partitioning(parts, hotspots)

            # update cache: remove keys not matching any current part sets (keep caches for unions)
            new_cache = {}
            # keep cached entries whose keys are subsets of current parts union or exact matches
            current_universe = set()
            for p in new_parts:
                current_universe.update(p)
            for k, v in cache.items():
                if k.issubset(current_universe):
                    new_cache[k] = v
            cache = new_cache
            parts = new_parts
            # ensure at least one part exists
            if not parts:
                parts = [customer_nodes]

            iter += 1

        # final decode: ensure incumbent exists
        if incumbent is None:
            # fallback naive packing
            solution = [0]
            cur_load = 0
            for i in range(1, n):
                if cur_load + self.demands[i] > self.vehicle_capacity:
                    solution.append(0)
                    cur_load = 0
                solution.append(i)
                cur_load += self.demands[i]
            if solution[-1] != 0:
                solution.append(0)
            return solution

        # final repair to be safe
        final = self._project_and_repair(incumbent)
        # ensure format: flat list
        return final

def _two_opt(self, tour, iters=1000, time_limit=None):
    # Optimized in-place 2-opt improvement on tour (list)
    # Uses local variables to minimize attribute lookups and reduces overhead in inner loop.
    if tour is None or len(tour) < 4:
        return tour
    # Ensure mutable list
    tour = list(tour)
    dm = self.distance_matrix
    n = len(tour)
    start_time = time.time()
    iter_count = 0
    improved = True
    # Outer loop controls number of improvement passes
    while improved and iter_count < iters:
        if time_limit and (time.time() - start_time) > time_limit:
            break
        improved = False
        # For each edge (a-b) try to find a non-adjacent edge (c-d) that yields improvement
        # Access dm rows once per fixed node to reduce indexing cost.
        for i in range(n - 1):
            a = tour[i]
            b = tour[i + 1]
            d_a = dm[a]          # row for a
            d_b = dm[b]          # row for b
            dab = d_a[b]         # distance a-b (constant for this i)
            # j ranges avoid adjacent edges and maintain cycle correctness
            j_end = n if i > 0 else n - 1
            for j in range(i + 2, j_end):
                c = tour[j]
                dnode = tour[(j + 1) % n]
                # d_c = dm[c]  # only fetch when needed
                # delta = (dm[a, c] + dm[b, dnode]) - (dm[a, b] + dm[c, dnode])
                # Using cached rows:
                delta = d_a[c] + d_b[dnode] - dab - dm[c, dnode]
                if delta < -1e-9:
                    # perform reversal of segment (i+1 ... j) inclusive
                    # slice-reversal is implemented via [::-1] which is efficient in CPython
                    tour[i + 1:j + 1] = tour[i + 1:j + 1][::-1]
                    improved = True
                    break
            if improved:
                # After an improvement, restart scanning from the beginning for best effect
                break
        iter_count += 1
    return tour

# Your key function here
def _solve_subproblem_greedy(self, nodes):
    # Solve VRP on given nodes (list of customer indices, excluding depot 0)
    # Return list of routes, each route is list of nodes starting and ending with depot 0
    if len(nodes) == 0:
        return []
    # first-fit decreasing by demand (pack nodes into routes)
    nodes_sorted = sorted(nodes, key=lambda i: -self.demands[i])
    routes = []
    loads = []
    for node in nodes_sorted:
        placed = False
        for r_idx, load in enumerate(loads):
            if load + self.demands[node] <= self.vehicle_capacity:
                routes[r_idx].append(node)
                loads[r_idx] += self.demands[node]
                placed = True
                break
        if not placed:
            routes.append([node])
            loads.append(self.demands[node])

    # order nodes within each route by a vectorized nearest-neighbor heuristic starting from depot
    final_routes = []
    for r in routes:
        if not r:
            continue
        r_arr = np.array(r, dtype=int)
        visited = np.zeros(len(r_arr), dtype=bool)
        seq = [0]
        cur = 0
        # use numpy vectorized distance lookups to pick nearest unvisited efficiently
        while not visited.all():
            # get distances from current node to all nodes in this route
            dists = self.distance_matrix[cur, r_arr]
            # mask already visited with +inf so argmin ignores them
            # (works even if distance_matrix is float)
            masked = np.where(visited, np.inf, dists)
            idx = int(np.argmin(masked))
            next_node = int(r_arr[idx])
            seq.append(next_node)
            visited[idx] = True
            cur = next_node
        seq.append(0)
        final_routes.append(seq)
    return final_routes

algorithm RecursivePartitionCoordinator(problem, params)
    parts ← Partition(problem, params.initial_partitioning)                       // spatial/structural decomposition
    cache ← InitCache(); incumbent ← null; iter ← 0
    while not Terminate(iter, params)
        sub_solutions ← ∅
        for each part in parts
            sub_solutions[part] ← cache.get(part) or SolveSubproblem(part, params.subsolver) // exact/heuristic per part
        boundary_model ← BuildBoundaryModel(parts, sub_solutions, problem)       // small meta-instance linking parts
        coordinator_decision ← SolveCoordinator(boundary_model, params.coordinator) // flow/matching/assignment
        candidate ← AssembleSolution(sub_solutions, coordinator_decision)
        candidate ← ProjectAndRepair(candidate, problem)                         // global feasibility projection
        candidate.score ← Evaluate(candidate, problem); incumbent ← Best(incumbent, candidate)
        hotspots ← DetectFailureOrHighCostZones(candidate, problem)              // where decomposition hurts
        if ConvergedOrLimitReached(incumbent, iter, params) then return Decode(incumbent, problem)
        parts ← AdaptPartitioning(parts, hotspots, params)                       // split/merge/refocus regions
        UpdateCache(cache, parts, sub_solutions); iter ← iter + 1
    end while
    return Decode(incumbent, problem)
